turns.assessment: The simultaneous ~5.5 dB power reduction on every channel of S14→S04 is already present at the input of booster oms.S14-S04.amp0 and then propagates through all downstream amplifiers. Stable pump currents and equal input/output reductions argue against amplifier gain or pump faults, while a span fault cannot explain the low booster input. This localizes the fault to the OMS input patch at S14; recent maintenance there further supports connector contamination rather than a hard disconnection.

proposals.rationale: A contaminated S14 ROADM-to-booster patch causes an all-channel soft power reduction at the booster input, matching the persistent ~5.5 dB drop throughout S14→S04 and the downstream OSNR/BER degradation. The signal is attenuated rather than lost, and S14 had recent maintenance.
